new.q: A 45-year-old male presented with cough and haemoptysis for 3 months. He also complained of evening rise of temperature and weight loss. Chest X-ray shows an upper lobe cavitary lesion and sputum is positive for acid-fast bacilli. morphological features.
Enumerate the factors contributing to the development of an infarct.

A 35-year-old female is suffering from high-grade fever, disorientation, hypotension, feeble pulse and features of multi-organ failure. What is your provisional diagnosis? What investigations will you suggest for this case?
